text.p: Journeyman golfer Domingo Hospital of Spain upstaged the early big-name stars with a seven-under- par 65 in the first round of the Desert Classic on Thursday, then expressed delight at the return of compatriot Jose Maria Olazabal.
But a 75-minute delay at the start of play because of fog left it unlikely that Olazabal could complete his round before darkness set in.
Olazabal is returning to competition after an 18-month break caused by foot problems which for a time left him unable to walk and threatened him with life in a wheelchair.
But treatment from a German doctor for a bio-mechanical problem brought about a recovery leading to his comeback this week.

Hospital, a 38-year-old from Barcelona who finished 37th on the European money list last year, had seven birdies and did not drop a shot on the 7,102-yard Emirates course, which played shorter than its distance in hot sunshine.
Afterwards he spoke of the concern Spanish players had for Olazabal.
"We thought he had no chance of coming back. People were saying he had no chance of walking again," Hospital said.
"Of course we're very pleased. We thought he would finish in a wheelchair. We figured he'd never come back again.
"I used to phone him once or twice a month. He tried to sound optimistic, saying he felt much better, but you felt it was just words.
"The pain was unbelievable for him just to stand. When you saw that, you thought he had no chance."
Olazabal's problems were diagnosed as rheumatoid arthritis in both feet until the German doctor provided a different diagnosis and prescribed exercise and physiotherapy as a cure.
Defending champion Colin Montgomerie and German Bernhard Langer were the other big names among the late starters.
World number one Greg Norman compiled a one-under-par 71 despite hitting into water twice on his first nine holes -- the back nine of the course -- and dropping shots.
"I made a couple of mental errors but I'm pleased with my first tournament round in three months," he said.
"I could have shot 67, I played well enough. But I didn't make a lot of putts, which was to be expected after the break.
"I'll probably get progressively better each day here," said Norman, who began his break after winning his fifth Australian Open title in November.
Welshman Ian Woosnam had a late bogey in a three-under 69 while European Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros dropped three shots on his last two holes for a 74.
